title: Operator upgrade fallback orchestrator and tenant state safeguard
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers experienced partially-applied operator upgrades in Private/VPC clusters when maintenance windows overlapped with node drains. The half-applied upgrade left operator CRs in a migrated-but-uninitialized state, corrupted the on-disk KV index for tenant manifests in a handful of cases, and caused request retries and tenant-facing errors. This ticket delivers a fallback orchestrator that coordinates staged upgrades, atomic manifest checkpoints, automated safe-rollbacks, and an emergency remediation script for corrupted tenant KV indices.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New orchestrator component can coordinate a staged upgrade and pause mid-upgrade to ensure no tenant CR remains half-migrated; 2) Upgrades can be safely rolled back automatically when node drains or webhook failures exceed threshold; 3) Provided remediation script restores tenant KV index from last checkpoint for at least 98% of simulated corruption cases; 4) Customer-facing runbook and postmortem prepared and reviewed by SRE and Support; 5) New flows covered by automated integration tests and e2e in a synthetic tenant cluster.
work_log: 2025-02-18 - Priya Kapoor: Ticket opened after Support escalation from 2 enterprise customers (ACME Analytics, GreenWave Health). Initial summary of incidents attached. Observed pattern: operator upgrade started, node drain unexpectedly interrupted webhook handshake, CR migration partially wrote new schema and left index pointers inconsistent.

2025-02-19 - Liam Chen: Reproduced partial migration locally by simulating SIGTERM to operator during CRD reconcile. Confirmed KV index divergence when reconcile stopped between checkpoint and finalization. Created spike branch operator/upgrade-orchestrator-spike. Created integration harness to simulate rolling node drains.

2025-02-20 - SRE (Ana Morales): Collected telemetry from affected tenants: increased reconcile latencies, missing manifest entries, increased 5xx to tenant control-plane during window. Created dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/upgrade-fallback (internal).

2025-02-22 - Engineering meeting: Decided approach: implement an orchestrator sidecar inside operator control-plane that (a) snapshots manifest diffs before upgrade step, (b) acquires cluster-scoped coordination lease, (c) exposes progress checkpoint to allow safe-resume or rollback. Trade-offs: modest added complexity vs high reduction in customer-impact and manual restores.
design_notes: Checkpoint model: store manifest diffs in Minio-backed store with TTL 14 days; manifest diffs are signed and compressed. We will avoid storing secrets by omitting Secret objects — only metadata and CR status diffs.

Coordination protocol: use leader-election + per-tenant fencing token to avoid parallel upgrades colliding across namespace boundaries. Fencing token implementation leverages existing lease CRD to keep changes Kubernetes-native.

Rollback strategy: orchestrator will attempt three-step recovery: 1) idempotent replay of last good manifest checkpoint; 2) orchestrated operator restart on a drained node set; 3) if replay fails, run index-repair job that scans manifest keys and rebuilds KV index based on WAL and checkpoint snapshots.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): Complete operator/upgrade-orchestrator-spike branch, add simulated failure/recovery tests (done).
Phase 2 (core): Implement checkpoint store and fencing lease; add orchestrator lifecycle hooks; expose HTTP endpoints for progress and abort (ETA 4 days).
Phase 3 (safety): Build index-repair job and remediation script; integration test against 10 synthetic tenants with induced corruption (ETA 2 days).

Phase 4 (rollout): Canary rollout to non-prod then to 3 pilot customers with telemetry gate and automatic abort on increased reconcile errors. Prepare customer communication templates and Support playbook (ETA 3 days).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Checkpointing may capture sensitive data. Mitigation: Filter secrets; only capture CR metadata, status, and non-sensitive spec fields. Add review by Compliance.
Risk: Orchestrator lease could become single point of failure. Mitigation: Use Kubernetes leases with automatic failover; design for leader re-election and idempotent checkpoints.

Risk: Index repair may be slow for large tenants. Mitigation: Throttle repair job, run at low-priority QoS, and provide progress to customer. Consider snapshot-based fast-restore for very large tenants.
Risk: New HTTP endpoints increase attack surface. Mitigation: endpoints authenticated via operator client certs and internal network only; validate requests and add audit logs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint creation/restore and fencing token lifecycle.
Integration tests that simulate SIGTERM during each phase of CR migration and assert safe rollback with no tenant data loss.
Chaos test: randomly kill operator pod during canary upgrade and assert orchestrator either resumes or restores to last good checkpoint.
Performance test: measure checkpoint store overhead (target < 2% CPU/memory increase on control-plane).
customer_communication_and_runbook: Initial outreach: Support to notify impacted customers with timeline and remediation steps (template: https://docs.google.com/document/d/upgrade-outreach-template).

Runbook: Step-by-step customer runbook added: 1) Pause upgrades by labeling tenant namespace with upgrade.pause=true; 2) Run repair job: kubectl apply -f repair-job.yml --namespace operator-system; 3) Monitor dashboard and escalate to SRE if repair takes >2 hours.

current_blockers: Waiting on Compliance sign-off for checkpoint retention policy (Ana Morales assigned).
Storage: Need an S3-compatible bucket in Private deployments; infra team reviewing costs and isolation requirements.
Large-tenant performance: need additional benchmark runs to validate repair job runtime on tenants with >1M manifest entries.
